column1: # OWASP ZAP baseline — passive-scan rule tuning (OSE-1186 G2).
# Format (tab-separated, EXACTLY 3 columns):  <ruleId>
# The 3rd column is an info message (ZAP uses only id+action; the name is for
# humans) and is REQUIRED — a 2-column line fails config load. The full reason
# lives in the `#` comment directly above each override; an IGNORE without a
# written reason is a review smell, the same way a skipped test is.
# First run: 0 FAIL, 8 WARN categories across 10 public surfaces, 59 PASS.
# The Worker's HTML pages correctly emit CSP (nonce), X-Frame-Options, nosniff,
# Referrer-Policy and HSTS — all PASS. What remains splits into verified noise
# (IGNORE below) and real hardening gaps (left as WARN — visible, tracked, not
# yet gating; see the "REAL GAPS" note at the bottom).
# ── VERIFIED NOISE — IGNORE (each checked, not blanket-suppressed) ──
# [10031] "User Controllable HTML Element Attribute (Potential XSS)" on
# /forms/:id?type=... — FALSE POSITIVE, verified in src/handlers/form-pages.ts:
# the `type` param only selects a switch branch (line 530); it is never
# interpolated into the output. The submitForm() calls use hardcoded literals
# ('register','checkin','survey','email-signup'), not the raw param. Reflected
# XSS is impossible-by-construction here.

column3: User Controllable HTML Element Attribute (Potential XSS)
